title: Compatible arrows of descent data descend from a universally descending refinement
statement:
Work with quasi-separated schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-quasi-separated-morphism] and their fibre products [def-pc-fibre-product] in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $\mathcal G$ be a contravariant category-valued pseudofunctor: it assigns a category $\mathcal G(V)$ to each such scheme, pullback functors $h^*$ to maps, and natural isomorphisms $(hk)^*\cong k^*h^*$ and $\mathrm{id}^*\cong\mathrm{id}$ satisfying the associativity and unit identities. Its fibres need not be groupoids. For $p:U\to S$, let $\operatorname{Desc}_{\mathcal G}(p)$ have objects $(A,\alpha)$ with $A\in\mathcal G(U)$ and $\alpha:\mathrm{pr}_1^*A\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathrm{pr}_2^*A$ on $U\times_SU$, identity on the diagonal and satisfying $\alpha_{23}\alpha_{12}=\alpha_{13}$ on $U\times_SU\times_SU$; an arrow $u:(A,\alpha)\to(B,\beta)$ is an arrow $u:A\to B$ satisfying $\beta\,\mathrm{pr}_1^*u=\mathrm{pr}_2^*u\,\alpha$, with all comparisons inserted. Call $p$ universal descent if the canonical functor $\mathcal G(V)\to\operatorname{Desc}_{\mathcal G}(U\times_SV\to V)$ is fully faithful for every quasi-separated $V\to S$. Let $U\xrightarrow{a}Y\xrightarrow{b}S$ be maps of quasi-separated schemes, and suppose $ba$ is universal descent. Then restriction along $a$ induces a fully faithful functor
$$a^*:\operatorname{Desc}_{\mathcal G}(b)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Desc}_{\mathcal G}(ba).$$
Thus for every two $b$-data, every compatible arrow between their restrictions lifts to a unique compatible arrow between the original data. No descent or surjectivity assumption is imposed on $a$, and no object-effectivity hypothesis is imposed on $ba$.

source.place: Proposition (5.6), printed p.19: supporting Hom descent for the refinement assertion; construction supplied by Q09, not stated separately in the paper. Read online; local copy WANTED.

proof.text: Put $p=ba$ and $W=U\times_SY$, with projections $t:W\to U$ and $q:W\to Y$. All products and the graph $s=(\mathrm{id}_U,a):U\to W$ exist by [def-pc-fibre-product]. They stay in the quasi-separated domain: a map from a quasi-separated scheme is quasi-separated, this property survives base change, and a quasi-separated map to a quasi-separated scheme has quasi-separated source, by clauses (1)-(3) of [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence], using the scheme convention in [def-weil-quasi-separated-morphism]. Apply this successively to the products below. For each quasi-separated $V\to S$, the assumed fully faithful comparison for $U\times_SV\to V$ says exactly: an arrow between pullbacks of two objects of $\mathcal G(V)$ lifts uniquely if its two pullbacks to the kernel pair agree. In particular pullback along this projection is injective on arrows between these objects. This is the assumed Hom bijection, with no effectiveness assertion.

source.place: Proposition (5.6), printed p.19, Hom-only refinement input; explicit argument by Q112 (not a separately stated result of the paper)

proof.text:
Fix two $b$-data $(A,\alpha),(B,\beta)$ and an arrow $v:a^*A\to a^*B$ of their restricted $p$-data. For maps $x,y:T\to Y$ with $bx=by$, write $\alpha_{x,y}:x^*A\to y^*A$ for pullback of $\alpha$ along $(x,y)$, and likewise $\beta_{x,y}$. Products written as tuples below denote projection maps of schemes, not evaluations on geometric points. Insert the given pseudofunctor comparison isomorphisms in every composite; their associativity and unit identities allow reassociation of these expressions. Thus $\alpha_{y,z}\alpha_{x,y}=\alpha_{x,z}$ and $\alpha_{x,x}=1$, and likewise for $\beta$. On $W$, define the actual arrow
$$h=\beta_{at,q}\,t^*v\,\alpha_{at,q}^{-1}:q^*A\longrightarrow q^*B.$$
The isomorphisms inverted here are descent isomorphisms; the arrow $v$ itself need not be invertible.

source.place: Proposition (5.6), printed p.19, Hom-only refinement input; explicit argument by Q112 (not a separately stated result of the paper)

proof.text:
Check the kernel-pair condition for $h$ over $Y$. On $W\times_YW=U\times_SU\times_SY$, label the projections $(u_1,u_2,y)$ and abbreviate $\alpha_{a u_i,y}$ to $\alpha_{iy}$ and $\alpha_{a u_1,a u_2}$ to $\alpha_{12}$; use analogous notation for $\beta$ and put $v_i=u_i^*v$. The compatibility of $v$ pulled back from $U\times_SU$ is $\beta_{12}v_1=v_2\alpha_{12}$. Consequently
$$h_2=\beta_{2y}v_2\alpha_{2y}^{-1}=\beta_{2y}\beta_{12}v_1\alpha_{12}^{-1}\alpha_{2y}^{-1}=\beta_{1y}v_1\alpha_{1y}^{-1}=h_1.$$
The last equality uses the two displayed cocycle identities of step 2. Hence $h$ is an arrow between the canonical $q$-descent data of $A,B$. Step 1 with $V=Y$ supplies a unique $f:A\to B$ with $q^*f=h$. Pull back this equality along the graph $s$: since $qs=a$, $ts=\mathrm{id}_U$ and both diagonal descent isomorphisms are identities, it yields $a^*f=v$.

source.place: Proposition (5.6), printed p.19, Hom-only refinement input; explicit argument by Q112 (not a separately stated result of the paper)

proof.text:
It remains to verify that $f$ is a $b$-datum arrow. Put $Z=Y\times_SY$. The projection $r:U\times_SZ\to Z$ is a base change of $p$, so is injective on arrows by step 1. On its source use projection labels $(u,y_1,y_2)$; the maps $(u,y_i)$ to $W$ pull $q^*f=h$ back to $f_i=\beta_{u i}v_u\alpha_{u i}^{-1}$, where the index $u$ in a descent isomorphism means $a(u)$. The two sides of the desired equation satisfy
$$\beta_{12}f_1=\beta_{12}\beta_{u1}v_u\alpha_{u1}^{-1}=\beta_{u2}v_u\alpha_{u1}^{-1},$$
$$f_2\alpha_{12}=\beta_{u2}v_u\alpha_{u2}^{-1}\alpha_{12}=\beta_{u2}v_u\alpha_{u1}^{-1}.$$
Here $\beta_{12}\beta_{u1}=\beta_{u2}$ and $\alpha_{12}\alpha_{u1}=\alpha_{u2}$ are the cocycles on $Y\times_SY\times_SY$, pulled back along $(a(u),y_1,y_2)$. Faithfulness for $r$ gives $\beta\,\mathrm{pr}_1^*f=\mathrm{pr}_2^*f\,\alpha$ on $Z$.

source.place: Proposition (5.6), printed p.19, Hom-only refinement input; explicit argument by Q112 (not a separately stated result of the paper)

proof.text:
For uniqueness, any compatible $g:A\to B$ with $a^*g=v$ satisfies, on $W$,
$$\beta_{at,q}\,t^*(a^*g)=q^*g\,\alpha_{at,q}.$$
Thus $q^*g=\beta_{at,q}t^*v\alpha_{at,q}^{-1}=h=q^*f$. Injectivity in step 1 for $V=Y$ gives $g=f$. This proves bijectivity on each Hom set. Restriction is a functor because pullback preserves identities and composition, and pulling the datum equation back along $a\times_Sa$ preserves it. Therefore the restriction functor is fully faithful. The only inverses used were $\alpha^{-1},\beta^{-1}$, so this argument applies to arbitrary fibre categories and arbitrary arrows. All appeals to universal descent were at $V=Y$ or $V=Y\times_SY$; no property of $a$ and no realization of any object was assumed.
